name: bridge-tally
description: Ask about the TallyPrime books on this computer, and prepare Journal, Payment, Receipt and Contra vouchers as a local file. Posting is off until you turn it on below; then it posts one voucher at a time, each after you approve it in a native dialog. What it reads, amounts included, goes to your AI provider; Response redaction can only shorten party and ledger names and bank account numbers or drop narrations.
long_description:
ComplyEaze Bridge lets Claude Desktop read the TallyPrime books on your own computer. It is built for chartered accountants, CA firms and accountants. You can ask about the trial balance, outstanding receivables and payables with ageing, ledger movement and vouchers, the purchase and sales registers and the stock summary, and have it prepare Journal, Payment, Receipt and Contra vouchers as a local file.

Posting to Tally is off until you turn it on in this extension's settings. When it is on, each voucher is posted only after you approve it in a window on your computer.

What Claude reads from your books goes to your AI provider as part of the chat, including company, party and ledger names, amounts, dates, narrations, references, GSTINs and, when it reads ledger details, PAN, bank account numbers, IFSC, MSME or Udyam registration numbers, email, phone and address, and, when it builds a voucher file, that file's local path (which can include your computer user name). The Response redaction setting takes one value, not both: it can shorten party and ledger names and bank account numbers, or drop narrations. It does not hide amounts, company names, PAN, GSTIN, IFSC, MSME or Udyam registration numbers, contact details or references, and a shortened name can still be identified, not least from the GSTIN or PAN sent beside it.

ComplyEaze Bridge talks to TallyPrime's own XML gateway on a loopback address, so it cannot be pointed at a remote Tally host (it cannot tell whether that local port is forwarded to another machine; on a Mac, TallyPrime runs in a Windows virtual machine with its port forwarded to the Mac). It is packaged for Windows x64 and Apple Silicon Macs, and has not been run in MCP clients other than Claude Desktop. ComplyEaze Bridge is open source under the Apache License 2.0 and is not made by or affiliated with Tally Solutions.

accept_terms_2026_10_1.description: Tick to use ComplyEaze Bridge: it refuses every tool call until you accept the Terms of Use. Terms: https://bridge.complyeaze.com/terms. Privacy: https://bridge.complyeaze.com/privacy.

host.title: Tally host
host.description: Where Tally runs on this computer: localhost, 127.0.0.1 or ::1.

port.title: Tally port
port.description: Tally's HTTP port on this computer.

redaction.title: Response redaction
redaction.description: What to hide from your AI provider: none, mask_parties (shortens party and ledger names and bank account numbers to their first two and last two characters) or drop_narration (removes narrations). Neither hides amounts, company names, PAN, GSTIN, IFSC, MSME or Udyam registration numbers, contact details or references. Any other value stops the connector from starting.

enable_writes.title: Allow voucher posting (Journal, Payment, Receipt, Contra)
enable_writes.description: Off by default. When on, ComplyEaze Bridge can post one Journal, Payment, Receipt or Contra into Tally at a time (or a batch, if batch posting is also allowed), each only after you approve it in a separate window. Leave it off unless you accept the known limits in Terms of Use section 9.2 (Posting), including these four: 1) Tally picks the company by name. A company renamed to, or opened under, that name (or one differing only in capitals or spaces) right after the last check could still receive the voucher. ComplyEaze Bridge may flag it afterwards, but cannot always say where the voucher went, and cannot prevent it. 2) A ledger renamed and replaced in that same moment can receive the post instead. It is marked for checking when seen, but not every such change is seen. 3) There is no undo: a wrong post must be corrected by hand in Tally. 4) The approval window covers only ComplyEaze Bridge: another Tally connector in the same Claude Desktop that can change entries can do so without it. You can also record, in another window, that you reviewed a voucher marked for checking; that writes nothing to Tally. Reading, bank-statement parsing and voucher file preparation work either way.

enable_batch_post.title: Allow posting a batch of up to 50 vouchers under one approval
enable_batch_post.description: Off by default, and used only when voucher posting is on. When on, one approval can post a saved batch of 2 to 50 Journals, or of 2 to 50 Payments, Receipts and Contras, in one import. The approval window then shows a summary: the totals for each ledger, with a line for each voucher only when there are 10 or fewer. Leave it off unless you accept these known limits, beyond those of voucher posting: 1) If Tally creates only some vouchers of a batch, ComplyEaze Bridge reports which ones it finds in the book and which it does not, and refuses to post the missing ones again: check each in Tally. 2) A batch of more than 50, or one whose summary does not fit the window (about 20 ledgers), is refused: prepare it in parts, for example a bank statement by date range.
